source: U.S. National Library of Medicine, The Visible Human Project (public domain), male and female CT and cryosections via the NCI Imaging Data Commons; lower-limb geometry Andreassen et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:34, doi:10.1038/s41597-022-01905-2 (CC BY 4.0). Derived data, measured by the named script.
_README: Height correction of the Visible Human female cryosection frame (scratchpad vh_cryo_f/cryo_frame_*.npy, 1 mm slices in her torso-CT RAS z, frame.json z0 -1776). Measured 2026-09-13 by scripts/cryo/vhf_check_frame_z.py (pixel-wise fat/muscle Dice of each CT slice against the photographs; table in vhf_cryo_frame_z_survey.json): frame v1 was 47-90 mm too HIGH over the whole body below the neck (its z line had been fitted with the thorax anchors left out), i.e. slice k of v1 showed the anatomy of k - offset. scripts/cryo/vhf_correct_frame_z.py rewrote the frame with that offset (v1 kept as *_v1.npy; frame.json 'z_correction'), so scripts reading the frame need NO further shift: the values below are zero for the corrected frame and exist so lean_envelope.frame_y_correction() stays a no-op unless a future survey finds a residual.
